title: THE SEVEN SEALS
mv: For the great day of his wrath is come; and who shall be able to stand?
mvp: “For the great day of his wrath is come; and who shall be able to stand? Revelation 6:17
assignment: Highlight the theme of the third seal to the seventh seal (2x5=10 Marks).

b.x: There are three series of end-times judgements from God: the seven seals (Revelation 6:1-17; 8:1-5), seven trumpets (Revelation 8:6-9:21; 11:15-19), and seven bowls/vials (Revelation 16:1-21). As the end times progress, the judgements get increasingly worse and more devastating. The seven seals, trumpets and bowls are connected to one another. The seventh seal introduces the seven trumpets (Revelation 8:1-5), and the seventh trumpet introduces the seven bowls (Revelation 11:15-19; 15:1-8). The focus of this lesson is to learn what each of the seven seals symbolises and understand their significance.
The First Seal - The White Horse (Revelation 6:1-2)

This represents the Antichrist, who comes appearing as a source of peace but is intent on conquest. The crown symbolises authority and the bow suggests military aggression; his true intention is to conquer.
The Second Seal - The Red Horse (Revelation 6:3-4)
This symbolises war and bloodshed. Peace is taken from the earth, resulting in widespread conflict and violence.
The Third Seal - The Black Horse (Revelation 6:5-6)
This represents famine and economic hardship. Food is scarce and expensive, with rationing and inflation indicated by the scales.
The Fourth Seal - The Pale Horse (Revelation 6:7-8)
This brings Death, followed by Hades. One-fourth of the world's population dies through war, famine, plague, and wild beasts.
The Fifth Seal - The Cry of the Martyrs (Revelation 6:9-11)
This reveals those martyred for their faith. They cry out for justice but are told to wait until the full number of martyrs is complete.
This marks great upheaval: a massive earthquake, darkened sun, blood-red moon, falling stars, and the displacement of landforms. People hide in fear of God's impending wrath.
The Seventh Seal - Silence and Preparation (Revelation 8:1-6)
This opens with silence in Heaven, symbolising awe or anticipation. It introduces the Seven Trumpets. Prayers ascend to God before more judgements begin.

i: Initiate the end-time judgements leading into the Great Tribulation (Revelation 22:11-12).
Reflect both spiritual truths and physical consequences (Revelation 1:1).
Serve as a call to repentance and a warning to the unfaithful (Revelation 2:16).
Encourage faithfulness and perseverance among believers (Revelation 2:10).
Emphasise God’s complete sovereignty over history and destiny (Revelation 1:8).

b.x: Ultimately, the Seven Seals reveal God's justice, mercy, and authority.
The seventh seal introduces the seven trumpet judgements. Do not wait to experience these judgements. Stay rapturable!
